key_insight: A recursive deep-learning pipeline can replace slow finite-element simulations to rapidly predict how plant fibers deform and carry stress under transverse compression.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-throughput mechanical screening of realistic natural-fiber geometries, supporting faster design of sustainable composite materials.
method: Two coupled recursive U-Nets predict step-by-step deformation and internal stress evolution.
A regression CNN estimates transverse Young's modulus from the final stress field.
The model is trained on 1,000 synthetic hemp-fiber geometries with FE ground truth.
evidence_signal: On the abstract-reported test results, the stress-field sequence was reproduced with SSIM 0.9574 ± 0.0074 and RMSE 0.0345 ± 0.0079, while modulus prediction achieved R² = 0.938 ± 0.024, MAE = 24.31 ± 1.23 MPa, and MAPE = 5.25 ± 0.91%.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on synthetic fiber geometries derived from hemp cross-sections, so robustness to unseen species, manufacturing defects, and broader loading conditions still needs validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
